entities.label: Person
entities.summary: Gaucelm Faidit was a troubadour, born in Uzerche, in the Limousin, from a family of knights in service of the count of Turenne. He travelled widely in France, Spain, and Hungary. His known patrons include Geoffrey II, Duke of Brittany and Dalfi d'Alvernha; he was also at one time in Poitiers at the court of Richard I of England, for whose death he wrote a famous planh (lament) in 1199. It is possible, though controversial, that Gaucelm took part in the Third Crusade from 1189–1191; it seems clear that in 1202 he set out on the Fourth Crusade, as did his then-patron, Boniface of Montferrat, but after 1202 there is no further historical trace of Gaucelm.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: As a troubadour and poet of the medieval era, Gaucelm Faidit's travels and patronage had significant regional impact in France, Spain, and Hungary. His work, including his famous planh for Richard I of England's death, provides insight into the cultural exchange and politics of the time.
